competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: The payroll and wage upside surprise may lift expected policy rates and discount rates, creating a headwind for risk-sensitive assets including XRP.
support: BLS reported 165k payroll growth versus pre-release estimates of 59k to 65k.
BLS reported 0.4% monthly and 3.1% annual average hourly earnings growth.
Financial Times reported the two-year Treasury yield rose 6 basis points to 4.53% and the dollar strengthened.
counterevidence: The unemployment rate was little changed at 4.1%.
Labor-force participation and the employment-population ratio changed little.
Part-time employment for economic reasons rose by 339k to 4.8M, indicating remaining labor-market slack.
No synchronized XRP event-time return, cross-asset regression or control series is available.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Stronger hiring may support income and economic activity, partly offsetting higher-rate pressure on risk assets.
support: Payroll gains exceeded both retrieved pre-release estimate sources.
counterevidence: Average hourly earnings accelerated to 0.4% month over month.
Secondary market reporting describes higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: The prior technology-led selloff and broader deleveraging may explain more of XRP weakness than the employment release.
support: The November 5 risk-off session preceded the November 6 BLS release.

counterevidence: No synchronized BTC, equity-index, rates, FX and XRP event study has been run for this window.
